facts.fact: Africa50 and Bayobab (MTN Group) announced a partnership in May 2023 to co-develop Project East2West, a terrestrial fibre network of up to about US$320-325 million linking landlocked countries to east and west coast subsea cables, with Zambia listed among the countries covered and Africa50 investment committee approval on 21 July 2023.

systems.platform: terrestrial fibre optic cable (dark and active fibre)
systems.owner: Bayobab (MTN Group), majority sponsor, with Africa50

slug: 2025-01-20 PID Appraisal Stage - Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (P505094)

facts.fact: The World Bank's project information document for the Digital Zambia Acceleration Project states that cross-border infrastructure between countries is missing in Zambia, hindering seamless digital trade; the document is dated 20 January 2025 and gives no earlier date.

note: The project has a sub-component 'Extending the backbone and regional network' (IDA US$20m, commercial US$10m) but the excerpt names no cross-border link or other country at its end.
Online sale piloted in Zambia and verification data sharing concern a motor insurance scheme; no shared link or facility is agreed, built or in service.

facts.fact: MZ News reports that on 20 February 2026 the Mozambique-Zambia Interconnectivity Project was launched at Cassacatiza with Zambia's science and technology minister present, a cross-border fibre partnership of Vodacom Moçambique and Bayobab Zambia with both countries' regulators involved.

note: Launch ceremony only; works begun or in service not stated.
Angola only says it is interested in a fibre link to Zambia; no facility named.

facts.fact: ITWeb Africa reports that Zambia and Burundi signed an MoU at the Digital Government Africa Summit in Lusaka for a fibre cable under Lake Tanganyika linking Zambia's Northern province to Burundi's Makamba province, with a private firm, not yet named, contracted.

note: An exchange-point list; states no agreement between national bodies or a regional programme.

facts.fact: Bayobab Zambia and Vodacom Moçambique, with officials of both countries present, launched a fibre interconnection at the Zambia-Mozambique border on 2026-02-21, with infrastructure sharing.

note: One company's network across borders, with no arrangement between national bodies stated.
